Residuals of a fitted model, one per individual

Source: R/check-hazard.R
hazard_residuals.Rd

Computes a randomised residual for each individual, in the manner of the simulation-based residuals of the DHARMa package: the position of what was observed within what the fitted model predicts for that individual. When the model describes the data, the residuals are uniform between 0 and 1.

Usage

hazard_residuals(fit, n_draws = 400)

Arguments

fit

A brmsfit, a model fitted with fit_hazard().

n_draws

A single number, the number of posterior draws to average the predicted survival over, evenly spaced through the posterior. Defaults to 400.

Value

A tibble with one row per individual: id; path_id; the variables of the model that have one value per individual (covariates and groupings); time, the time at which it failed or was last observed; Ta, the temperature at that time; event, 1 for a failure and 0 for a survivor; and residual.

Details

The residual is the fraction of individuals that the model predicts to have failed by the time this one did, 1 - S(t), with the individual's own covariates and the group-level effects estimated for its groups, averaged over the posterior draws. A residual near 0 is an individual that failed earlier than the model predicts, and one near 1 an individual that lasted longer. What is observed is not always a single time, so the residual is drawn at random within what was observed:

  • a failure at a known time has the residual 1 - S(t);

  • a failure known only to an interval has a residual drawn uniformly between that fraction at the start of the interval and at its end;

  • a survivor, known only to have outlasted its last observation, has a residual drawn uniformly between that fraction at its last observation and 1.

The draws are random: call set.seed() first for the same residuals again. One residual per individual is used, and not one per interval, because the intervals of an individual are slices of one exposure and are not separate observations.

The residuals are to be examined against what was set before the outcome was known: a covariate, a treatment, a trial. They should not be examined against the time of failure, or the temperature at failure in a ramp. An individual that failed late has, by that fact alone, a high predicted fraction failed at its time of failure, so the residuals rise with the time of failure under any model, right or wrong.

References

Hartig, F. (2024). DHARMa: Residual diagnostics for hierarchical (multi-level / mixed) regression models. R package version 0.4.7. doi:10.32614/CRAN.package.DHARMa

See also

plot_residuals() to draw them, check_survival() for a check by group.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
set.seed(1)
res <- hazard_residuals(fit)
plot_residuals(res)                      # against the uniform distribution
plot_residuals(res, against = "trial")   # by trial
} # }
